newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TENNIS-ONDRUSKA WIN PUTS S.AFRICA AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ONDRUSKA WIN PUTS S.AFRICA AHEAD.

text.p: South African number two Marcus Ondruska gave his country a surprise 1-0 lead by beating Russian number one Andrei Chesnokov in the opening singles of their Davis Cup world group, first-round tie on Friday.
The 24-year-old Ondruska, world-ranked 103, overcame the Russian 7-6 6-3 3-6 4-6 7-5 after nearly four hours in temperatures of up to 41 degrees Celsius at the Westridge Park Stadium.
"That's one of the toughest matches I've ever played -- it was incredibly humid out there," Ondruska said afterwards.
The 73rd-ranked Chesnokov, who clawed his way back from two sets down, also felt the heat.
"I felt like dead meat on the court -- the heat was terrible," Chesnokov said.
The fifth set began with an exchange of breaks before both players held serve to reach five-all.
Chesnokov then double-faulted at 30-40 down in the 11th game to give Ondruska a 6-5 lead and the South African, playing with increased confidence, held his serve to take the set and the match.
World number eight Wayne Ferreira was meeting Andrei Cherkasov in Friday's second singles.
